name: QR Code Scams
summary: A fraudulent QR code placed over a real one sends your payment to a criminal or your details to a phishing page.

typicalLoss.note: Amounts vary from small parking payments to full account compromise where the code leads to a fake banking login.

howItWorks.detail: A fraudulent QR code is printed and placed over the legitimate one on a parking meter, restaurant table, poster or donation stand. It looks entirely native.
A QR code is unreadable to a human. There is no way to tell by looking whether it points where it claims to.
Either the payment goes to the criminal's wallet, or the code opens a cloned banking or payment login that harvests credentials and OTPs.
For small payments, most people never check. For phishing variants, the account compromise shows up days later.

redFlags: A QR sticker that is misaligned, raised at the edges, or clearly stuck over something else.
The page it opens asks you to log into your bank rather than simply to pay.
The recipient name shown in your app does not match the business.
A QR code in an unsolicited email, SMS or letter.
Being asked to scan a code to 'verify' or 'release' something.
illustrativeCase: QR stickers are placed over the payment codes on parking pay stations in a coastal town. Hundreds of small payments of R20 to R60 go to a criminal's wallet over a long weekend, and dozens of motorists also receive fines because the actual parking was never paid.
howToProtect: Always check the merchant name and amount shown in your app before confirming a QR payment.
Feel the code. A sticker over a printed surface is usually detectable with a fingernail.
Never log into banking through a QR code. Legitimate QR payments do not require a banking login.
Prefer paying inside, at the till, or through the venue's own app.
Be sceptical of QR codes on posters, flyers and unsolicited post.
ifYouveBeenHit: If you paid the wrong recipient, report to your bank immediately and request a recall.
If you entered banking credentials, phone the fraud line and change your password from a clean device.
Tell the business or municipality so the fraudulent sticker is removed.
Open a SAPS case, particularly where a public site was tampered with.

faqs.q: Can a QR code itself contain a virus?
faqs.a: Not directly. It contains a link or payment instruction. The risk lies entirely in where it sends you and what you do there.

faqs.q: How do I check a QR code before scanning?
faqs.a: Most phone cameras preview the destination address before opening it. Read that preview, and stop if the domain is not what you expect.
